newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs steady-off $1 - dealers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs steady-off $1 - dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices early Thursday were steady to $1.00 per cwt lower, with most of the weakness in the western corn belt amid more than adequate hog receipts, livestock dealers said.
Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota hogs sold $1.00 lower at $58.00 to $59.00 in the country and $60.00 to $60.50 at plants, the dealers said.
Illinois hogs sold steady to $0.50 lower at $59.00 to $59.50 in the country and $60.00 to $60.50 at plants, although some packers indicated they would pay $61.00 for top quality hogs, sources said.
Indiana hogs sold $0.50 lower at $58.50 to $59.00 in the country and $59.00 to $59.50 at plants. Declines were blunted by heat-related light movement, Indiana hog buyers said.

Ohio hogs were steady at $58.00 to $59.00 in the country and $60.00 to $61.00 at plants, with prices underpinned by ongoing light marketings in part due to extreme heat and humidity, livestock dealers said.
"The heat was bearable yesterday (Wednesday) because there was not much humidity, but its real bad this morning," one Ohio hog source said.
